Short answer: Yes — if the supply is to customers in Ireland, the standard Irish VAT rate is 23% and that is still correct as of today (September 4, 2026). ([revenue.ie](https://www.revenue.ie/en/vat/vat-rates/search-vat-rates/current-VAT-rates.aspx?utm_source=openai))

Two quick important caveats you should consider before sending the PDF:
- If the digital service is supplied to consumers located in another EU Member State, VAT is due at the consumer’s local (destination) rate under the OSS rules — so you would not charge Irish 23% for EU customers in other countries. ([vat-one-stop-shop.ec.europa.eu](https://vat-one-stop-shop.ec.europa.eu/national-vat-rules/ireland-vat-rules_en?utm_source=openai))  
- Some specific supplies (printed books, certain health products, etc.) may be zero‑rated or have different treatment; electronically supplied services are generally taxable at the standard rate unless a specific exemption applies. ([charteredaccountants.ie](https://www.charteredaccountants.ie/taxsourcetotal/2010/en/act/pub/0031/notes/sec0091-1-notes.html?utm_source=openai))

If you’d like, I can:
- Draft a one‑line clarification to insert in the PDF (to cover the destination‑rule nuance), or  
- Update the PDF text for you now (tell me how you want the note to read).
